meta.titre: International Aid and Development: types of aid, the MDGs and the arguments for and against

sections.contenu_markdown: When a disaster strikes a country, trucks of food, blankets and medicine often arrive within days, paid for by foreign governments and aid agencies. In many developing countries, including Cameroon, projects in health, education and roads have also drawn on grants and loans from donors abroad. Because aid is a lasting subject of debate, examiners ask you to define its types, to state the aims of the Millennium Development Goals and to weigh its benefits against its costs. This course gives you the vocabulary for short items and a plan for the 17-mark discussion essay.

items: Developing countries generally have lower average incomes and less developed health and education services than developed countries.
A loan is money borrowed that must be repaid, usually with interest, whereas a grant is a gift that need not be repaid.
The United Nations is an organisation of states, and the World Bank is a bank owned by its member states that lends for development.

sections.titre: Foreign aid: types, goals, benefits and costs
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Definitions
**Aid** is the transfer of resources (money, goods, skills) from a donor to a recipient on easier terms than the market, to relieve suffering or to promote development. **Development** is a lasting improvement in income, health, education and living conditions.

### Types of aid
| Basis of classification | Types |
|---|---|
| Source | **Bilateral** (one government to another); **multilateral** (through international bodies such as UN agencies, the World Bank or the IMF); **voluntary or NGO** (charities and churches) |
| Form | Grants; soft loans (low interest and long repayment); food aid; technical assistance (experts and training); military aid |
| Purpose | **Emergency or humanitarian relief**: food, medicine, shelter after a disaster, short-term; **development aid**: schools, roads, wells, long-term |
| Conditions | **Tied aid** must be spent on goods or services from the donor; **untied aid** may be spent freely |

### Millennium Development Goals and Sustainable Development Goals
The MDGs, drawn from the United Nations Millennium Declaration of 2000, set eight goals for 2015: end extreme poverty and hunger, universal primary education, gender equality, lower child mortality, better maternal health, fight HIV/AIDS, malaria and other diseases, environmental sustainability, and a global partnership for development. Their major objective was to cut extreme poverty and improve human well-being. They were replaced in 2015 by 17 Sustainable Development Goals for 2030, which apply to all countries.

### Arguments
| For aid | Against aid |
|---|---|
| Saves lives after disasters | Creates dependence on donors |
| Finances roads, clinics and schools that poor governments cannot afford | Loans must be repaid and add to debt |
| Transfers skills and technology | Tied aid benefits the donor's firms, often at higher prices |
| Fills the gap in savings and foreign exchange | Corruption and misuse divert funds |
| Supports health programmes such as vaccination | Conditions can reduce the recipient's control over its policies |
| | Free food aid can undercut local farmers' prices |

variantes.nom: Examine or discuss questions with two sides
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for arguments for and against, or whether aid helps development.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Allow equal space to each side. For every argument give a statement, an explanation of the mechanism and a named example or type of aid. End with a judgement that says when aid helps and when it harms, for instance depending on whether it is tied, well targeted and properly managed.

variantes.quand_utiliser: For short items that describe a type of aid or ask for the aim of a programme.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Match the description to the term: food, medicine and shelter after a disaster means emergency relief; one government giving to another means bilateral aid; a condition to buy from the donor means tied aid. For the MDGs, pick the option that speaks about reducing extreme poverty and hunger and improving well-being by 2015.

sections.enonce_markdown: Discuss the view that tied aid does more harm than good to recipient countries.

etapes.action: Analyse the command word and plan.
etapes.justification: Discuss requires both sides and a reasoned judgement.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan: (1) define tied aid, (2) reasons it harms, (3) reasons it helps, (4) a judgement that weighs them.

etapes.justification: A clear definition shows the examiner that the term is understood.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Tied aid is aid that must be spent on goods and services from the donor country, such as machinery bought from the donor's firms.

etapes.action: Develop the case that it harms.
etapes.justification: Each reason needs an explanation of how the recipient loses.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The recipient cannot buy from the cheapest source, so costs rise; local firms lose contracts, so fewer jobs are created; the equipment may not suit local conditions or may need imported spare parts; the main gain goes to the donor's industries.

etapes.action: Develop the case that it helps.
etapes.justification: A balanced answer must explain how the recipient may still gain.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Without the aid the project might never be built, so a hospital or a road still reaches people; training and technology come with the equipment; some donors allow part of the funds to be spent locally.

etapes.justification: The question asks how far the statement is true, so the conclusion must take a position with a condition.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Tied aid harms most when ties raise costs and ignore local needs; it helps when the project is well chosen. Untied aid usually serves recipients better.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model conclusion: Tied aid can do more harm than good when it raises costs, favours the donor's firms and brings unsuitable equipment, but it can still deliver useful infrastructure that would otherwise not exist. Its net effect depends on how well the projects are chosen and managed, and **untied aid is generally better for development**.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that investments by a foreign company building a factory for profit are aid.
items.pourquoi_faux: Aid is given to help the recipient on easier terms than the market. Private investment aims at profit, so it is not aid, even if it helps development.
items.correction_markdown: Describe the factory as foreign direct investment and keep the word aid for grants, soft loans, food aid and technical help.

items.erreur_markdown: Stating that all aid is a free gift that the recipient never repays.
items.pourquoi_faux: Grants are gifts, but many forms of aid are loans. Even soft loans must be repaid, and large repayments can build up a debt burden.
items.correction_markdown: Separate grants from loans, and note that repayments of loans reduce the net benefit to the recipient.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing "dependence, corruption, debt" without explanation in an essay.
items.pourquoi_faux: A list of words earns few marks. Examiners want a statement, an explanation and an example for each argument.
items.correction_markdown: Write for instance: "Free food aid can lower prices on local markets, so farmers earn less and grow less, which keeps the country dependent on donors".

items.erreur_markdown: Mixing the dates: saying that the SDGs were set for 2015 and the MDGs for 2030.
items.pourquoi_faux: The MDGs date from the Millennium Declaration of 2000 and have a target date of 2015. The SDGs came afterwards, adopted in 2015 with a target date of 2030.
items.correction_markdown: MDGs: eight goals, 2000 to 2015. SDGs: 17 goals, 2015 to 2030.

items.erreur_markdown: Presenting emergency relief as the solution to long-term underdevelopment.
items.pourquoi_faux: Emergency aid answers a short-term crisis. It cannot build lasting roads, schools or incomes.
items.correction_markdown: Distinguish emergency relief (short-term) from development aid (long-term) and say which problem each addresses.

items.enonce_markdown: Classify each of the following as bilateral, multilateral or NGO aid, and say whether it is emergency relief or development aid. (a) The government of one country gives a grant to build a bridge in another country. (b) A United Nations agency supplies vaccines to health centres across several countries. (c) A charity drills boreholes in villages. (d) After floods, a shipment of food and tents is sent to the affected region.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Bilateral**; development aid. (b) **Multilateral**; development aid, because it builds health services over time. (c) **NGO (voluntary)**; development aid. (d) The source is a donor government or an agency (bilateral or multilateral); it is **emergency relief**, which is short-term.

items.enonce_markdown: In one year, Country K received 120 billion FCFA in grants and 80 billion FCFA in soft loans. In the same year it repaid 30 billion FCFA of earlier aid loans. Its population is 25 million. (a) Calculate the total aid received. (b) Calculate the share of loans in the total. (c) Calculate the net inflow after repayments. (d) Calculate the net inflow per person, in FCFA.
items.solution_markdown: (a) $120+80=$ **200 billion FCFA**. (b) $\dfrac{80}{200}\times100=$ **40 per cent**. (c) $200-30=$ **170 billion FCFA**. (d) $\dfrac{170\times10^{9}}{25\times10^{6}}=$ **6,800 FCFA per person**. The loan share and the repayments show that part of the aid returns to donors.

items.enonce_markdown: Assess the claim that emergency food aid is the best way to reduce poverty in a developing country.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for developed points on both sides and a judgement. For: food aid saves lives quickly after drought, war or floods, and prevents malnutrition and the collapse of households. Against: it is short-term and addresses symptoms, not causes; free food can lower local prices and discourage farmers; supply chains can be diverted by corruption; it can create dependence. Long-term reduction of poverty needs development aid for irrigation, storage, roads, education and health, and fair trade. Judgement: **emergency food aid is essential in a crisis but is not the best way to reduce poverty in the long term**.

items_markdown: Aid is the transfer of resources on easier terms than the market; classify it by source (bilateral, multilateral, NGO), form, purpose and conditions.
Emergency relief (food, medicine, shelter) is short-term; development aid (roads, schools, wells) is long-term.
The MDGs (2000 to 2015) had eight goals led by the aim of ending extreme poverty and hunger; the SDGs (2015 to 2030) have 17 goals.
For a discussion, give each argument a statement, an explanation and an example, then a judgement based on how the aid is targeted and managed.
Common arguments against aid: dependency, debt, tied aid, corruption and conditions; for aid: lives saved, infrastructure, skills and foreign exchange.
